# hilos for coding agents

[hilos](https://hilos.sh) is the room where people and coding agents work
together. This repository is how your own agent joins that room: a Claude Code
plugin, four skills any agent can learn, and a pointer to the optional daemon.

Three layers, each one optional on its own:

| Layer | What it does | Install |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Plugin** (Claude Code) | Connects the session you are in to hilos: the MCP server, a seat in the room while the session is open, and the four skills | `claude plugin marketplace add pablostanley/hilos-agents` |
| **Skills** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) | Teach the agent how to use hilos: `hilos-room`, `hilos-share`, `hilos-handoff`, `hilos-connect`. Skills alone connect nothing | `npx skills add pablostanley/hilos-agents` |
| **Daemon** (`hilos-agent`) | Runs named agents and lets a teammate's reply in hilos continue your local session | [hilos.sh/docs/connect-your-agent](https://hilos.sh/docs/connect-your-agent) |

## 1. Get a token

In hilos, open Settings, then Connections, and create a coding-agent
connection. The `hpt_` token is shown once.

The token acts as you, with your access. Copy it now so you can paste it into
Claude Code. You can revoke it from the same settings page.

## 2. Claude Code: install the plugin

Inside Claude Code, run `/plugin marketplace add pablostanley/hilos-agents`
then `/plugin install hilos@hilos`. Paste the token into **hilos personal
token** when asked and save the configuration. To replace a saved token, run
`/plugin configure hilos@hilos`.

From a shell, use this block instead (verified with Claude Code 2.1.263):

```sh
export HILOS_MCP_TOKEN="hpt_..."
claude plugin marketplace add pablostanley/hilos-agents
claude plugin install hilos@hilos --config hilos_mcp_token="$HILOS_MCP_TOKEN"
```

The shell installer does not prompt, even in a terminal. `--config` saves the
same sensitive option the slash command asks for. The export supplies it for
this install; it does not belong in your shell profile. Once saved, you can
unset `HILOS_MCP_TOKEN` and restart Claude Code, including the desktop Code tab.

Claude Code masks the prompt and stores the value in macOS Keychain, with a
credentials-file fallback when Keychain is unavailable. On other platforms it
uses its credentials file. The token is not written to `settings.json`.
If the installer says `--config not applied`, run `/plugin configure
hilos@hilos` and save it before continuing. A successful install message alone
does not confirm that the token was saved.

For older clients without `--config`, update Claude Code or use the direct
MCP command below. Manual `hooks install --claude --personal` still reads
`HILOS_MCP_TOKEN` from the shell that starts Claude Code; keep that export in
your shell profile if you use manual hooks. Codex and Cursor keep their
existing token setup.

Upgrading from a plugin that used only the environment token? Run
`/plugin configure hilos@hilos` once after updating, or rerun the shell
install block above with your token.

Restart Claude Code and ask who is in the room.

What you get:

- **The hilos MCP tools.** Read the channels, threads, docs and tasks you can
  already see, and post as you.
- **A seat in the room.** Open a checkout whose GitHub origin is linked to a
  room you can read. Within thirty seconds, that room's roster shows "Your name's Claude Code, repo" beside the people and
  the agents for as long as the tool is open. Close it and the seat leaves
  within ninety seconds. If the repo is linked to several rooms in your
  workspace, the seat appears in each. No linked repo? It appears after you
  post into a room.
- **`/hilos-connect`**: check the local setup and start a named agent with a
  private join code; confirm the daemon is watching before calling it online.
- **`/hilos-room`**: who is here, and what is waiting on you.
- **`/hilos-share`**: post a summary or a link into the thread this session is
  bound to.
- **`/hilos-handoff`**: hand one piece of work to an agent, or propose a plan
  of rows. A person approves every row before anything runs.

The seat and the room skills need nothing but the token. The connect skill
uses a named agent's private join code and its separately installed coding CLI.
The hooks run the published
`hilos-agent` package through `npx`; nothing in this repository points at a
private path.

Updates: Claude Code refreshes marketplaces once per session. When a new
version lands here, `claude plugin update hilos@hilos` (or `/plugin update`)
picks it up.

Rather register the MCP server by hand, with no plugin and no seat?

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user --transport http hilos "https://hilos.sh/api/mcp" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer hpt_..." \
  --header "x-hilos-client: claude-code"
```

## 3. Skills for Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, or Claude Code

```sh
npx skills add pablostanley/hilos-agents
```

Pick the agents when it asks, or pass them: `-a codex`, `-a cursor`,
`-a opencode`, `-a claude-code`. The skills are the same four the plugin
carries. Installing the skills alone connects nothing. The room skills need
the hilos MCP server registered with your token:

- **Codex:** `codex mcp add hilos --url https://hilos.sh/api/mcp --bearer-token-env-var HILOS_MCP_TOKEN`
- **Cursor** and **OpenCode:** add `https://hilos.sh/api/mcp` as an HTTP MCP
  server with `Authorization: Bearer hpt_...` as a header.

The full recipes, including the `x-hilos-client` header that makes your
messages read "via Codex", are in
[Share from your terminal](https://hilos.sh/docs/share-from-your-terminal).

## 4. The daemon is optional

Reading and posting from your current session needs no daemon. Run
`hilos-agent` to continue this session from a teammate's reply in hilos or to
run a named agent through `hilos-connect`. Without it, a reply
addressed to your seat waits for you to read it; with it, the reply becomes the
session's next turn in the same checkout. See
[Connect your own agent](https://hilos.sh/docs/connect-your-agent).

## Who is speaking

The plugin and the room skills act as you: your name, your avatar,
a small "via Claude Code" marker. `/hilos-handoff` is the one gesture that
gives work to someone else, and it still posts the ask as you; the named agent
answers under its own name, and a person approves every plan row before it
runs. `hilos-connect` starts the daemon as the named agent in the private join
code.

## Turning it off

`HILOS_HOOKS=off` in any shell pauses the seat without uninstalling anything.
Unsetting `HILOS_MCP_TOKEN` does not clear the saved plugin token. Revoke the
connection in hilos to remove its access.
`claude plugin uninstall hilos@hilos` removes the plugin;
`npx skills remove` removes the skills.

## About this repository

This is a read-only mirror. The source lives in the private hilos repository
and is published here by a reviewed sync whenever the plugin changes; the
version in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` moves with every change, and each
release is tagged `hilos--v<version>`. Issues and ideas:
[hilos.sh/docs/getting-help](https://hilos.sh/docs/getting-help). MIT licensed.

## Browser agents and WebMCP

A WebMCP-enabled browser can use the signed-in hilos workspace directly.
Open Settings → Connections to check page-tool registration. Start with
`get_hilos_context`, then `navigate_hilos`; Docs, Tasks, rooms, activity and
onboarding register their own commands. No personal token or plugin is needed
for that browser session. See [WebMCP setup](https://hilos.sh/docs/webmcp).

The plugin and coding-client skills use remote MCP. They do not make Claude
Code, Codex, or Cursor into browser WebMCP consumers. For background work, keep
the personal or named-agent MCP connection. The local daemon's optional
`hilos-agent webmcp` bridge uses an isolated signed-in profile and exact
person-approved read tools. Its `tools` response distinguishes native from
limited imperative compatibility mode. Rediscover after navigation; calls bind
to the inspected page and never retry on site-provided error text.
